Header: Redwood All-Hands - September 2026
Date: 2026-09-28
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 75 minutes
Attendees (key): Maya Patel, Priya Nair, Liam O'Sullivan, Sofia Chen, Carlos Rivera, Anya Malik + All Employees (remote)

Summary (auto): Q3 wins, product milestone shifts, Optimize feature demos, hiring and security note.

00:00 - Maya Patel: good morning everyone uh, thanks for joining the september all hands, hope folks in apac had a smooth start, we'll run about an hour and change, stick around for q and a.
00:18 - Priya Nair: quick ops note, the runtime team landed the attention kernel patch, we're seeing 8 to 12% token throughput improvement on long sequences, this will help Dedicated latency targets.
00:36 - Sofia Chen: yeah, and to add, the change improves memory behaviour with kv cash -- sorry k v cash in some of the transcriptions so it's spelled odd in the notes, but the KV cache eviction logic also tightened up.
01:05 - Maya Patel: awesome. on the biz side, q3 usage was up 42% month over month in enterprise accounts, revenue ahead of plan by about 9%, big shout to growth and se for onboarding the three large healthcare pilots.
01:30 - Anya Malik: real quick, APAC uptake doubled after the singapore region launch, we need to follow up with localized docs and a replay for that timezone.
01:48 - Carlos Rivera: product roadmap — small change: Dedicated GA originally target was late october, moving to mid-november to get the final SLA tests in. we want to avoid a rushed GA.
02:10 - (murmurs) Speaker 1: will that affect pricing?
02:16 - Liam O'Sullivan: short answer no; pricing comp remains the same, but the committed capacity contracts will have a slightly adjusted timeline clause. legal's stamping it this afternoon.
02:40 - Priya Nair: tech update — Optimize is shipping a cost-aware batching suggestion engine; it's been reducing per-token cost in our internal trials by ~18% for medium-length chat workloads. still some edge cases with very short prompts.
03:05 - Maya Patel: any red flags on quality regressions?
03:10 - Priya Nair: we've tied the quality monitor to prompt sets and evals; one false positive in reranker scoring, but rolling a fix. nothing customer-visible yet.
03:30 - Sofia Chen: engineering headcount — we hired 12 folks in q3, ramping SRE and runtime teams. next quarter focus is infra automation and Private deployment on-prem packaging improvements.
04:00 - (interruption) Speaker 2: sorry, can you repeat the private deployment note?
04:06 - Sofia Chen: sure, Private on-prem binary will include an optional control-plane stub for air-gapped installs, and fuller KMS/HSM integrations for customers who need HSM-backed keys. we're roadmapping it for q4.
04:30 - Maya Patel: security update from Lina (remote): SOC2 in progress, external audit scheduled for mid-october; ISO scope being finalized for europe customers.
04:46 - (slide flip) Speaker 3: question from chat: competition?
04:50 - Maya Patel: yes, we keep an eye on OpenAI and Anthropic, and on the infra side nvidia partnerships are important for kernel and optimizer collaboration. our angle is unified inference + cost controls.
05:12 - Carlos Rivera: demo time — quick run through of the Optimize UI: suggestions show batching, quant profiles, and model recommendations with estimated monthly $ savings. (audio: demo clicks) you can toggle workloads and see projected savings.
06:05 - (short pause) Speaker 4: transcribe glitch, demo was a bit fuzzy on the recording, we'll share the high-res clip.
06:20 - Priya Nair: technical callouts — need to schedule a kernel selection deep dive with partners, and finalize quantization profiles for the 8-bit path. some of the numbers still noisy due to sequence length distribution.
06:45 - Maya Patel: ok, we also have customer stories — healthcare pilot reduced inference cost per encounter by about 27% using caching + batching, great case study to push to marketing.
07:05 - Anya Malik: marketing will package that with a short write-up and a customer quote, need legal approval for the quote.
07:20 - (crosstalk) Speaker 5: question on SLA for Dedicated?
07:25 - Liam O'Sullivan: SLA will be 99.9% for Dedicated with latency SLO tiers; we'll publish the per-route latency breakdown in the console. rolling canaries during GA to validate.
07:45 - Sofia Chen: ops note — auto-scaling policy for Dedicated supports burst capacity config, but we need to expose a simpler UI to avoid misconfigurations. action item for product + eng.
08:10 - Carlos Rivera: hiring/org — we'll open two director-level roles for runtime and product security, details on careers page next week.
08:30 - Maya Patel: ok let's move to q and a. please keep questions high level; we'll route deep technical ones to the follow-up sessions.
08:45 - Q&A (various short questions):
09:00 - Speaker 6: what's the timeline for apac docs?
09:04 - Anya Malik: replay by 10/1 and localized docs by 10/10.
09:18 - Speaker 7: will private on-prem support multi-tenant inside customer infra?
09:22 - Sofia Chen: yes, it's optional — you can run isolated single-tenant or multi-tenant depending on the packaging and licensing.
09:40 - Speaker 8: can we see more details on the cost model?
09:45 - Carlos Rivera: yes, we'll share the unit economics spreadsheet and a sample pricing model for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private.
10:05 - Maya Patel: recap — thanks everyone, action items on the doc: roadmap deck, kernel deep-dive, Dedicated stress test, apac replay. we'll send recording and slides. next all-hands in mid-november, date tbd.
10:25 - (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription mis-heard some technical terms ("KV cache" as "K V cash" or "quant" as "quand"), speaker attributions generic in some parts. We preserved raw transcript feel with filler words and interruptions.
